notes:
## New features & enhancements

- **The first time, the control is a button rather than a switch.** A switch moves the moment you click it, while nothing has happened and the permission dialog is still open. A button has nothing to be wrong about.
- Once it has worked once it becomes an ordinary switch, because by then the asking is over. Nothing in the row moves when they swap: the button is the switch's exact size.
- The control never shows a state the machine has not confirmed. The line underneath says **Asking Windows…** until the shortcut actually appears.
- The note about the permission dialog is marked **IMPORTANT**, and goes away once you have dealt with it.
- The guide now explains the button, the dialog's two steps, and why the order matters — ticking **Always allow** after pressing Open is a tick made never.

## Bug fixes

- **The Start when you sign in switch did not work in 1.5.3.** Every flip really did change the Startup entry. What failed was the app looking again afterwards, so it put the switch back and said Windows had refused.
- The state was kept in a file the launcher writes once, at start. Nothing rewrote it after a flip, so the answer from launch came back and undid what had just happened. It now has its own file, written by whatever changes the entry.
- The app gave Windows 1.2 seconds to answer — less time than reading the permission dialog it had just opened. That is what flipped the switch to **off** behind that dialog, against a question nobody had answered yet. It now waits up to forty-five seconds, checking as it goes.
- The single check after the dialog closed raced a script that was still writing, so even a permission you granted could read as a refusal.
- The launcher wrote that file only after waiting for the radio's window, which in one case takes a full minute. It writes it before starting the browser now — measured at 0.6 seconds.
